content: Lamivudine, whether used alone or in combination with other antiviral medications, has the potential to cause severe liver damage and a condition known as lactic acidosis. If you experience symptoms such as an upset stomach, loss of appetite, extreme fatigue, weakness, dark yellow or brown urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, flu-like symptoms, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or pain in the upper right part of your abdomen, contact your doctor immediately. It is essential to keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to lamivudine. Epivir tablets and liquid formulations, which are used to treat human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), are not interchangeable with Epivir-HBV tablets and liquid formulations, which are used to treat hepatitis B infection. Epivir contains a higher dose of lamivudine than Epivir-HBV. Using Epivir-HBV in patients with HIV may make the HIV virus less responsive to lamivudine and other medications. If you are co-infected with HIV and hepatitis B, you should only take Epivir. If you are taking Epivir-HBV for hepatitis B, discuss your risk of HIV infection with your doctor. Lamivudine (Epivir) is prescribed in combination with other medications to treat HIV infection in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). However, it is not a cure for HIV or AIDS and may not reduce the number of HIV-related illnesses. Additionally, lamivudine does not prevent the transmission of HIV to others. Lamivudine (Epivir-HBV) is also used to treat hepatitis B infection. It belongs to a class of medications called nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, which work by inhibiting the spread of HIV and hepatitis B viruses. Lamivudine is available as a tablet and liquid for oral administration. Epivir is typically taken every 12 hours (twice daily), while Epivir-HBV is usually taken once daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take lamivudine exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking lamivudine even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Lamivudine is sometimes used in combination with zidovudine (Retrovir, AZT) to treat healthcare workers or others exposed to HIV through accidental contact with HIV-contaminated blood, tissues, or other body fluids. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Lamivudine may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking lamivudine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to lamivudine or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim, Septra) and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had hepatitis B, kidney disease, or (in children) pancreas disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking lamivudine, contact your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding is not recommended while taking lamivudine. If you miss a dose of lamivudine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Lamivudine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: diarrhea, headache, fatigue, chills, upset stomach, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, trouble sleeping, depression, stuffy nose, or cough. If you experience any of the following severe side effects or those listed in the Important Warning section, contact your doctor immediately: rash, stomach pain, vomiting (in children), upset stomach (in children), fever, muscle pain, or numbness, tingling, or burning in the fingers or toes. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store lamivudine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). The liquid form does not require refrigeration but should be stored in a cool place. Dispose of outdated or no longer needed medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
